subject: Configurable store regions + selective erasure: product Q&A & roadmap request
messages:
From: Ana Soto <ana.soto@edgebank.com>
To: rohan.mehta@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@edgebank.com
Date: 2028-08-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Quick Q: tenant-level region & selective erase for regulated data

Hi Rohan —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. A few follow-ups from our legal/security team about how Redwood would support EdgeBank's EU residency and GDPR workflows:

1) Can we pin a tenant to an EU-only storage region for all persisted artifacts?
2) Does Redwood support per-tenant TTLs that trigger automatic purge of embeddings/outputs?
3) We also need a selective-erasure flow (customer requested erasure of a subset of records) — can you describe the proposed UX + audit trail?

I’ve attached the list of questions the team compiled. We’re collecting the answers to decide between a hosted deployment vs. a dedicated/private option.

Appreciate any early clarity — tight timeline on our procurement (end of month).

Best,
Ana Soto
Senior Security Program Manager
EdgeBank

[Attachment: EdgeBank_Retention_Questions.pdf]

From: rohan.mehta@redwood.ai
To: Ana Soto <ana.soto@edgebank.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-08-15T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick Q: tenant-level region & selective erase for regulated data

Ana —

Thanks for the clear list and for flagging the timeline. High level answers here, and I’ll loop in product/eng for concrete roadmap items:

1) Tenant pinning: yes — we support region pinning at the tenant/workspace level in Private (VPC/on-prem) and Dedicated. For Hosted we offer region-residency options but not strict geo-lock today; we can describe contractual controls and routing to eu-west-1.

2) Per-tenant TTLs: planned. We have a design that allows a per-tenant retention TTL for persisted artifacts (embeddings, long-term cache). It’s not GA yet — engineering expects a staged rollout.

3) Selective erasure: we can support selective erasure with audit logs and erase-confirmation tokens. Current ask to product: add a selective erase endpoint (filter-based) + operator audit trail and a confirmation webhook for customers.

I’m attaching a quick matrix (proposed) for the options and the tradeoffs we think matter for procurement (latency, cost delta, compliance posture).

Next steps I propose:
- Marissa: can you own a short product note that spells the SLA/controls differences across Hosted/Dedicated/Private?
- Karthik: can eng estimate effort for tenant TTL + selective erase (filter-based) and the audit trail?

I’ll aim to have something to share by 2028-08-18 EOD.

Thanks —
Rohan Mehta
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: proposed-matrix-v1.csv]

From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai

On Wed, Aug 15, 2028 at 11:04 AM rohan.mehta@redwood.ai wrote:
> I’m attaching a quick matrix (proposed) for the options and the tradeoffs we think matter for procurement (latency, cost delta, compliance posture).

Folks —

Draft product note below (short form) that we can share with EdgeBank; please edit for accuracy:

- Hosted (standard): regional routing available by request; not strict geo-lock. Recommended for PoC where latency matters.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): tenant pinning to region is supported; data-at-rest in customer-dedicated GPU pools in specified region; can provide SOC2 evidence and longer audit retention.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): full geo-sovereignty; recommended for regulated banks. Includes KMS integrations and on-prem key storage.

Selective erasure & TTLs (proposal):
- Per-tenant TTLs: admin API to set TTL for persisted artifacts. Background purge job will respect SLA window (24–72hrs) and emit erase events to audit log.
- Selective erase endpoint: filter-based erase (e.g., document_id list or date range + namespace). Calls are soft-validated, then dispatched to purge pipeline with a confirmation token returned to caller.
- Audit trail: immutable events (erase-requested, erase-executed, erase-failed) with operator id and timestamp. Exportable via the Console and API.

Open questions for eng:
1) Can we guarantee immediate delete for hot cache + embeddings, or will KV/backup windows require a retention delta?
2) Estimated sprint-level effort for TTL + filter-erase + audit events.

If this reads OK I’ll share with Ana and call out GA timing as "targeted H1 2029" with a narrow beta earlier.

—Marissa
Director, Product Management
Redwood Inference

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, rohan.mehta@redwood.ai
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-08-17T14:40:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Quick Q: tenant-level region & selective erase for regulated data

Marissa / Rohan —

Thanks for the draft. Quick engineering read and estimate:

1) Tenant pinning: already supported for Dedicated (config + infra). Making Hosted geo-lock (hard guarantee) requires a routing+policy layer + contractual constraints with our cloud infra — low effort for a controlled region list, medium for legally enforced geo-lock.

2) Per-tenant TTLs: implementation plan — admin API + retention-config table + background purge worker. Blowups to watch: snapshot/backups and cold storage copies. We can aim for a beta that deletes primary copies within 24–72hrs; full deletion from backups/cold storage likely needs a separate workflow (compaction window).

3) Selective erase endpoint + audit trail: medium effort. Rough estimate: 3 sprints for a minimal safe pipeline (API, validation, purge worker, audit events). Add 1–2 sprints for console UX + exportable audit bundle. Need product to define the filter semantics strictly (IDs vs. fuzzy search ranges).

Risks/notes:
- Immediate/guranteed erase from GPU-resident caches is feasible; once data is replicated or backed up there is a compliance/process gap.
- For EU banking customers we should propose a Private deployment or Dedicated with contractual SLAs for backup purge windows.

I’ll add a short RFC in INF-873 and propose milestones (design, beta, GA).

—Karthik
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime

From: rohan.mehta@redwood.ai

Bcc: procurement@edgebank.com

Subject: Re: Quick Q: tenant-level region & selective erase for regulated data

Ana —

Appreciate the patience while we pulled this together. Short summary for your procurement/legal review:

- Tenant pinning: Dedicated (immediate) and Private (GA) — Hosted supports region routing but not strict geo-lock by default.
- Per-tenant TTL: we propose a configurable TTL in admin settings; beta targeted for Q4 2028 with GA in H1 2029. Primary-copy deletion goal: within 24–72 hours; backups/cold copies: separate purge SLA to be contractually defined.
- Selective erasure: we will provide a filter-based selective-erase API + operator audit events. Engineering estimate: ~3 sprints for API+pipeline; +2 sprints for Console + exportable audit bundle.

Next steps:
1) Marissa will share the short product note and the small matrix (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) by EOD tomorrow.
2) Karthik will open INF-873 with the RFC and a milestone plan; we’ll invite EdgeBank to a technical review once the RFC is ready.

If this looks acceptable I can route a procurement-friendly summary for signatures.

Thanks again —
Rohan Mehta
Head of Sales Engineering
